text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - serving-runtime-prod: GPU_ERROR/CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS on pool-gpu-us-west-2 (alert_id=INC-8421)

sara: seeing repeated container restarts on node-13 and node-14, OOM + illegal memory access in the runtime loader. hit rate ~2% of requests, visible 503s from edge. logs attached.

sara: logs (snip):
```
[2026-03-15T19:02:11Z] runtime: panic: cuda: illegal memory access
  at runtime/kernel.c:0x4f3b
  stack: launch_kernel -> kv_cache_handle -> tensor_write
[2026-03-15T19:02:11Z] containerd: oom_killer invoked, pid=8421, rss=38.2GiB
```

ben: acknowledged, I'm oncall. first pass: cordon node-13, drain non-critical pods, mark as investigating. tagging infra team.

matt: @ben do we have a quick fallback? can we route traffic to dedicated fallback model variant (cpu-quant) so customers see degraded perf but no 503s?

ben: yes — enable runtime fallback route policy. doing now.

ops-bot: action: set-route-fallback serving-prod -> model-variant/cpu-quant (policy_id=rf-77) by ben at 2026-03-15T19:05:22Z

aliya: customer-impact scoreboard: 3 customers with >2% errors, a handful of short-lived 5xx spikes in public telemetry. product notified. preparing customer messages. @cust-notify-bot will draft.

cust-notify-bot: Draft queued: "We're observing degraded availability for short windows on hosted inference due to GPU node failures; we've enabled fallbacks and are working on a kernel-level mitigation. We'll update within 60m."

kai: grabbing GPU node debug logs and nvminer traces now. suspecting a pagetable race in the kernel module when the runtime triggers heavy prefix-KV cache churn.

james-sre: any recent infra changes? kernel updates, driver rollouts, or hotpatches?

matt: we rolled driver nvidia-525.104 yesterday to 60% of nodes as part of perf rollout. could be correlated.

ben: rolling back driver on affected nodes to 525.89 (previous stable) as a mitigation plan. will patch one node at a time and validate.

sara: while rollback runs, i'm tuning the serving runtime: lowering max_batch_size to 8 and disabling aggressive prefetch to reduce KV churn. config snippet:
```yaml
runtime:
  max_concurrent_batches: 48
  max_batch_size: 8
  kv_prefetch: false
```

kai: attaching nvprof snippet showing memory access failure pattern (truncated):
```
GPU0: illegal memory access at 0x7f12ab3c, pc 0x7f12c1e4
backtrace: launch_kernel+0x34 -> execute_attention+0x1f0 -> kv_read+0x9c
```

matt: good. if rollback + runtime throttle clears, we'll keep fallback open for 30m before shifting traffic back gradually.

ops-bot: cordon node-13 executed by ben at 2026-03-15T19:08:40Z. draining in progress.

ben: rollback in progress on node-13 (ssh -> apt-get install nvidia-driver=525.89 && reboot). keeping node-14 isolated until we validate.

sara: quick check: redis eviction spiked when containers restarted, increased cache pressure. bumped redis maxmemory-policy to volatile-lru temporarily.

aliya: customer message sent to affected accounts (CS outreach). we flagged as incident for enterprise customers; outreach team on standby.

james-sre: monitoring kernel logs for pagewalk errors. adding increased log sampling on xvda and mgmt tooling.

ben: node-13 back up at 19:16, driver reverted, runtime svc restarted. initial smoke looks clean — no illegal memory access in last 2 minutes.

matt: traffic: rolling 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% planned, waiting 5m intervals. currently at 10% to node-13.

sara: telemetry: errors dropped from 2% to 0.15% after fallback + throttle. important metric: tail-latency increased ~60ms due to cpu fallback but overall success rate improved.

kai: nvminer traces on node-14 show early signs of the same pattern; keeping it cordoned until we revert and test. collecting core dump.

ops-bot: core-dump collected: /var/crash/runtime-gpu-2026-03-15-19:20-core.gz (uploaded to artifactstore/incidents/INC-8421/)

ben: decision log: immediate mitigation = enable fallback + throttle batches + rollback driver on affected nodes. medium-term: add kernel driver regression test and extend canary to 24h for driver rollouts.

aliya: customer impact update: errors subsided, most affected customers report restored traffic. will keep CS looped for 24h.

matt: executing canary test plan on node-14 after rollback. if clean, we'll uncordon and slowly lift fallback.

sara: note for postmortem: stack shows kernel pagewalk race leading to misaligned access in driver when KV cache eviction coincides with kernel map updates. need repro harness.

james-sre: @kai can you prioritize a deterministic repro using high-churn KV workload + driver instrumentation? I'll allocate two VMs.

kai: yes, starting that now. ETA 4-6h for initial repro attempt.

ben: handing incident to matt for follow-up and postmortem. i'm off for the night in 20m. status: mitigated, customer impact reduced, remediation tasks assigned.

matt: acknowledged. I'll own the postmortem and follow-through with driver vendor. opening follow-up ticket in tracker: INF-1134 (driver rollback policy + extended canary).

incident-bot: Incident INC-8421 status: Mitigated -> Follow-up. Handoff: ben -> matt at 2026-03-15T19:25:03Z.

sara: thanks team. will push a short incident note in #postmortems once we have kernel trace analysis. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder scheduled: postmortem draft due in 48h, severity: SEV2.

matt: closing thread for live mitigation. any immediate regressions, ping me directly.
